title: Rework anchored-spinner layering and icon tint fallback for compact button family
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problems surfaced by QA & early canary: (1) compact/icon-only buttons show a jitter when entering loading because spinner overlays are not anchor-aware; (2) icon tint falls back to an unreadable token in some dark-themes causing accessibility regressions; (3) press-hold / cancel interactions can leave a lingering spinner. This ticket captures a design spec to (a) introduce an anchored-spinner layer that reserves visual space and animates opacity rather than layout, (b) formalize icon tint cascade and token alias fallbacks for theme shifts, and (c) define press lifecycle edge cases and the graceful cancel escape hatch.
decision_notes: Prefer anchored spinner that occupies an invisible 24px anchor to avoid layout shift instead of toggling width/padding on state change.
Spinner will animate via opacity + transform (scale 0.92 -> 1) to reduce perceived jitter; motion-reduction setting must switch to fade-only.

Icon tint fallback uses token chain: component.icon-foreground -> component.surface-contrast -> semantic.high-contrast. This ensures readability when theme variables are missing or when quantized palettes are used.
We will not change existing HTML structure (button > icon/spinner) to avoid large engineering churn; instead CSS layering + aria-live region will be used for announcing loading state.
Added micro debounce (150ms) for transient loading states to avoid flashing spinner for very short interactions; documented UX tradeoff for perceived responsiveness vs flicker.
Accessibility: spinner presence must be exposed to screen readers via aria-busy / aria-live; text alternatives and focus behavior preserved for icon-only buttons.
Rollout: behind feature-flag 'anchored-spinner' for 2 releases to monitor regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Compact (24px) and icon-only buttons maintain stable layout when toggling loading state (no horizontal shift).
Icon tint cascade ensures 4.5:1 contrast against background in all Redwood-supported themes (light, dark, high-contrast).
Motion-reduced mode disables scale animation and uses only opacity transitions.
Spinner cancellation flow: if action canceled within debounce window, spinner never becomes visible; if canceled after spinner visible, spinner fades and no lingering focus trap remains.
Unit visual tests (Chromatic / Percy) added for default, dark, high-contrast, reduced-motion, and RTL.
Documentation updated: component README, tokens table, and example snippets for split-button / grouped icon cases.
Design sign-off from PM and Eng (UX review comment thread resolved) and a green e2e smoke test in staging.
tasks: Finalize anchored-spinner styles and token usage (design deliverable: Figma file + token table)
Create CSS spec for anchor box (24px) + spinner layering rules; document motion-reduction behavior
Work with Eng to add 150ms transient loading debounce and aria attributes
Add automated visual tests and manual QA checklist
Update component README + migration note for existing consumers
Create canary rollout plan and observability dashboard queries for button regressions
qa_notes: Test matrix: {variant: primary/ghost/compact/icon-only} x {theme: light/dark/high-contrast} x {motion: normal/reduced}.
Simulate transient server latency under 100ms to validate debounce hides spinner.
Verify keyboard focus remains visible during loading and that Escape cancels long-running simulated calls and removes spinner.
Run Chromatic snapshots and mark known differences; aim to keep visual diff under threshold for canary.
Coordinate with Eng to add a synthetic e2e that toggles loading rapidly to reproduce previous glitch.
accessibility_considerations: Use aria-busy on container and an offscreen live region to announce 'Loading' state for assistive tech.
Ensure icon-only buttons have accessible name (aria-label) and spinner does not steal focus.
Contrast validation for all token fallbacks; include test vectors in Confluence.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion by switching to opacity-only transitions and shortening timing functions.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature-flagged rollout to internal staging with visual tests (2 days)
Phase 2: Canary for 15% of production requests, monitor error/visual regression dashboard (1 week)
Phase 3: Full rollout and merge migration note; deprecate legacy spinner behavior after 2 releases
Rollback criteria: >0.1% increase in CSS rendering errors or >5 visual regression alerts on Chromatic baseline
